messages:
alex: Ran an nsys trace against prod-like load this morning, focusing on 8k seq, batcher window 12ms. Seeing a weird spike where queue_time >> compute_time for many requests, suspect KV prefetch pattern.
mina: Can you paste the nsys command and the top timeline snippet? :mag:
alex: command I used:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt -o run_prefetch --force \
  --capture-range=pid:12345:12345 ./stress_client --seq=8192 --qps=200
```
Top timeline: many small kernels (attention_fwd_small, softmax_small, kv_cache_lookup) interleaved with host->device memcpy; avg kernel duration ~0.6ms but launch gaps ~2.5-6ms.
jordan: So lots of kernel launch overhead because kernel_choice picked "small" kernels instead of fused larger ones? Did kernel_selection change last week? tess: We rolled a tweak that biases selection to reduce p99 memory use for smaller models. That might have regressed fused-kernel preference.
mike: I posted a perfetto link with full GPU slices: https://perfetto.redwood/run/abcd1234 (timeline highlights attached). It shows repeated memcpy peaks aligned with KV prefetch ops.
sre-bot: Automated regression detector flagged a +12% p95 tail for text-gen endpoint between 1784400000 and 1784480000.
mina: Interesting. Two hypotheses: 1) Batcher window too short causing many tiny dispatches; 2) KV prefetch is triggering synchronous memcpy per request (no async prefetch). alex: Agreed. I instrumented the runtime: when kv_prefetch_async=false we get those memcpys; with true, memcpy is moved earlier but still serialized because prefetch is triggered per-request before batching completes.
jordan: Could we instead prefetch once per batch (batch-level prefetch) and stash KV into shared GPU buffer before kernel launches? That would eliminate repeated memcpys.
tess: Worth trying. Also check kernel selection heuristic: if sequence_len > 2048 we should prefer fused_attention_large; looks like heuristic threshold wasn't applied for our model variant.
mike: Quick numbers from two runs I did:
- baseline (current): avg queue 4.6ms, avg compute 7.2ms, p95 latency 142ms
- batch-level-prefetch + enforce fused kernels: avg queue 2.1ms, avg compute 9.5ms, p95 118ms
So compute up but queue down and p95 improved ~17%.
alex: Nice. Recommendation: A/B rollout config: enable batch-level prefetch + force_fused_kernels for canary; monitor token-level cost change and p99.
mina: I'll file a small change to the batcher: move KV prefetch to post-batch-aggregation hook and add a flag `batch_prefetch=true`; also add telemetry to count per-request memcpy occurrences.
jordan: Also add a kernel-selection unit test to assert fused kernel choice for seq>=2048 with our model descriptor.
tess: I'll own the canary and dashboards. mike, can you add the perfetto & nsys snippets to the PR so reviewers can quickly eyeball timeline? mike: on it.
sre-bot: Canary policy created: route 5% of traffic to canary config; alert if p95 regresses >5% for 10 minutes.
alex: Thanks all — let's try to keep changes small and observable. If canary passes, plan for 2-step rollout: 20% -> 100% over 6h.
